Keep title “손이 기억하는” then “물건”, subtitle immediately below, date/place beside lower lock, hours in two lines after slash, free entry and intact URL. Keep the two large white hands outlined in black at their current positions: upper from LEFT grasping lever underside, lower from RIGHT pinching key bow. Keep continuous door edge, upper pivot, lower round rosette and their same-door functional relationship. Keep the clean white field without the earlier shadow below lower lock. Do not add any text, icon, arrow, fingerprint, ornament, logo, collection ID, sponsor or new historical fact.

CRITICAL LOCAL REPLACEMENT AT THE LOWER LOCK CENTER:
The supplied reference STILL has a rounded bulb and flared neck traditional skeleton-keyhole outline. Do not preserve that outline. Redraw that central area completely as a modern cylinder plug: a clean WHITE flat circular/oval plug inside the solid BLACK larger rosette, bounded by one thin black contour. In this white plug place a very NARROW BLACK rectangular/warded slit, with near-parallel sides. There is NO round bulb at its top, NO flared skirt, NO large empty opening under the blade. Fit this narrow slit to the key blade's thin entering edge. The existing key blade visibly enters the slit; hide its inserted tip behind the plug face at a crisp insertion boundary, leaving its exposed shaft and bow continuously connected. Keep the slight oblique view so one can read blade depth. A bitted everyday key with an intact round bow is pinched by thumb/index, with no extra fingers. The key is attached to the inserted shaft, not floating. The matching cylinder slit must read clearly at the 720px use view.

CRITICAL FLAT CONTACT WEAR:
The upper handle STILL has brushed/scratched/chipped white texture. Replace that textured band completely with one broad SOLID WHITE gently tapered curved contact-wear patch along the top of the BLACK lever, adjacent to the gripping hand. Make both edges continuous and smooth, without streaks, speckles, scratches, stipple, holes, gradients or gray modeling. Leave a solid black lever outer contour so the white patch reads as a worn metal surface, not a broken silhouette. Keep a sufficiently wide visible patch beyond the thumb. On the exposed key bow rim, keep one broad smooth WHITE arc where fingers repeatedly rubbed; make this a solid flat patch too. Other black surfaces remain solid black. Structural separation lines stay crisp and sparse. No gray cast shadows, no paper/metal grain, no modeled highlights apart from these intentional flat white contact areas.

The large hand actions must still be the substantive non-glyph center. Preserve the calm familiar everyday museum image and broad central-left reading space between them. The scene must not become an antique lock diagram or crime mood. This edit is limited to the observed lower keyway mismatch and remaining textured hardware wear; keep the earlier advantages of copy, contact gestures, layout and clean background.
